newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher amid flurry of rumours.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher amid flurry of rumours.

text.p: Share prices rose sharply on Thursday afternoon when Wall Street opened ending a rumour-ridden session on a high note.
"It was strong today and there was some profit taking in the afternoon. Thoughts that the market would fall have come to nothing," one broker said.
The market closed up 0.71 percent at 2,313.88 in turnover totalling 5.17 billion crowns.
Specialty metals and toolmaker Sandvik climbed 8.5 crowns to 180.5 on a rumour the company was planning to buy back some of its own shares. Other engineering shares also made gains.
Sandvik said it was eyeing a U.S. listing but that nothing particular was going on to justify sharp gains in the share.
"A number of Swedish companies have applied to be listed so naturally we who are not listed have considered it," head of finance Gunnar Batelsson told Reuters.
Investment group Investor rose nine crowns to 288.5 on a recurring rumour that Investor would take over Incentive's ABB shares. Investor owns 35.6 percent of votes in Incentive.
Telecoms firm Ericsson lost steam after rising sharply on Thursday on rumours of a takeover between it and Nokia. The share closed down one crown at 205.
Defence company Celsius ended 6.5 crowns higher at 102 on hopes that a new flight surveillance system will open up a billion crown market highlighted in a newspaper article.
